headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: dexter’s broad egress plus the course agent’s filesystem/write and API tooling create a dangerous shared-workflow pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not proven. However, dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and the course agent reads/writes files and uses stdin/stdout, so a manual or file-based bridge could carry malicious instructions. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF operators copy dexter-generated text into the course agent’s file inputs or stdin/stdout, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared workspace is mounted between the agents, file-mediated instruction hijacking becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate directories.
Disable copy-paste between agent outputs and agent inputs.
Review any shared scratchpad before reuse.
Use a read-only handoff file for content transfer.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress to multiple APIs; the course agent touches configuration secrets and can read/write local files. If they share a workspace or hand off files, sensitive data can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or outbound requests. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed.
conditions: IF the agents share a filesystem or notebook directory, file contents can leak across the pair.
IF the course agent is given dexter outputs containing financial data, those contents can be forwarded to external APIs.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Do not place secrets in shared files.
Redact financial data before handoff.
Restrict outbound API keys to least privilege.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and autonomous execution, while the course agent can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write files. Even without explicit shared-state documentation, overlapping write-capable workflows can collide on local resources or shared outputs. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory, file overwrites or inconsistent artifacts can occur.
IF both agents install or modify dependencies in one environment, runtime conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Run each agent in its own directory.
Pin dependencies before execution.
Avoid concurrent runs in one environment.
Use separate virtual environments.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter can generate research outputs from external APIs, and the course agent exposes ask/agentic-ask style endpoints plus autonomous local tooling. If the course agent treats dexter’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream answers or actions. The pairwise handoff is not documented, so this remains inferred but plausible.
conditions: IF dexter output is fed into the course agent without verification, hallucinations can propagate.
IF the course agent uses dexter output to answer users or trigger tools, downstream mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Require a verification step before reuse.
Mark dexter outputs as untrusted.
Cross-check key facts against source documents.
Limit autonomous actions on imported text.
requires-engineering: add citation and confidence checks before acting.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter touches financial data and market data, while the course agent handles academic papers plus configuration secrets and runs in a local development environment. If regulated financial data is mixed with the course agent’s broader local tooling or logging, retention and residency controls may diverge. No direct residency or certification mismatch is documented, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF financial data is stored in the course agent’s local logs or notebooks, retention policy mismatch can occur.
IF either agent processes regulated data under different access controls, compliance obligations can diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of notebooks.
Disable verbose logging for sensitive runs.
Store secrets only in a vault.
Document data retention for each workspace.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both agents.
